routes.description: Establish that a personal transcendent ground provides a unified explanation for the origin and order of nature, rational inquiry, biological information, objective morality, and the possibility of evil.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if these features require or are better unified by an intelligent, immaterial, morally sufficient ground and if objections from natural alternatives, moral relativity, and suffering do not defeat that comparison.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory inferences to theism as a more adequate account of reality than atheism.

centralBridges.description: Infer a transcendent intelligent cause from cosmic beginning, fine-tuning, and purposive order.
Ground trustworthy reason, scientific inquiry, and specified biological information in an immaterial intelligence.
Show that objective moral duties and human rights require a standard beyond individual or social preference.
Reconcile suffering with divine goodness through freedom, limited human knowledge, and the possibility of wider goods or justice.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish positive and potentially falsifiable design inference from an appeal based only on current ignorance.
Derive the relevant divine attributes from the kinds of effects the cumulative case seeks to explain.

routes.description: Establish that revisable natural inquiry and human responsibility explain or responsibly address reality without positing God, while testing theistic inferences against alternative accounts, contrary evidence, and suffering.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed divine explanation lacks sufficient evidential support or explanatory necessity, natural and social accounts remain viable, and the attributes assigned to God generate unresolved tensions with observed reality.

motionBridge.description: Connect evidential restraint, natural inquiry, and human responsibility to atheism as the better comparative approach to reality.

centralBridges.description: Show that unknown origins, observer selection, and inhospitable conditions do not warrant a transcendent designer.
Use cumulative evolution and established natural history as alternatives to sudden design and disputed creation accounts.
Account for moral judgment, empathy, and responsibility through human social life without an objective divine lawgiver.
Test omnipotence, foreknowledge, and benevolence against severe suffering and the claimed consequences of created freedom.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require independent evidence before treating an unexplained phenomenon as support for a law-transcending deity.
Assess whether scriptural moral and historical claims support the explanatory authority attributed to theism.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Fine-Tuning, and Design
sections.rationale: This issue tests the principal inference from the universe's beginning and apparent order to a transcendent intelligence against uncertainty, observer selection, and evidence of inhospitable or imperfect conditions.

sections.title: Reason, Knowledge, and Scientific Inquiry
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether rational and scientific practice requires an immaterial theistic foundation or can proceed through evidential restraint, revisability, and natural inquiry without that grounding.

sections.title: Biological Information, Evolution, and Natural History
sections.rationale: This issue compares intelligent-cause inferences from biological information with cumulative evolutionary explanation and examines how established natural history bears on creation claims.

sections.title: Morality, Empathy, and Human Responsibility
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether binding moral standards require a transcendent ground or whether social judgment, evolved empathy, and accountable human choice provide the relevant atheistic account.

sections.title: Evil, Suffering, Freedom, and Divine Responsibility
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether severe suffering is compatible with an omnipotent, omniscient, benevolent God and whether freedom, foreknowledge distinctions, wider goods, or human limits answer that challenge.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The universe's beginning and fine-tuning are best explained by a timeless, immaterial, uncaused intelligent creator.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Unguided materialism cannot justify trustworthy reason or free choice, whereas theism can ground rational thought.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: The information encoded in DNA points to an intelligent mind because meaningful codes arise from intelligent sources rather than repetitive natural forces.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Objective moral rights and wrongs require a standard beyond humanity, so atheism cannot justify objective morality or human rights.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: The reality of objective evil supports rather than defeats God's existence because evil presupposes objective good and an external moral standard.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Science depends on immaterial preconditions such as logic, causality, reason, free will, realism, orderly laws, and morality that theism explains better than atheism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Because nature began and is therefore an effect, its cause cannot be natural but must transcend space, time, and matter.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-08.proposition: Knowing a future action does not cause it, just as knowing a recorded game's result does not remove the players' freedom when they acted.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: Praise of honesty, justice, freedom, proof, and better choices presupposes objective standards that materialist atheism cannot supply.

chunk-004:c004-05.proposition: The design inference from biological information is falsifiable because natural production of specified complex messages would defeat the need for intelligence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Uncertainty about the universe's origin does not establish God, and exempting God from the origin question merely relocates rather than resolves the explanatory gap.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Admitting uncertainty about what preceded the Big Bang is more reasonable than asserting God, while explanations should remain responsive to verified physical inquiry and contrary evidence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Established evolutionary and stellar history conflict with a literal Genesis sequence and undermine the associated accounts of Eden, original sin, and the need for a savior.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Apparent order and the improbability of a particular observer do not establish design because observers necessarily assess the universe from rare conditions compatible with their existence.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-01.proposition: Evolution proceeds through retained incremental changes over immense spans of time, so an analogy to an instantaneous random spill misrepresents the proposed natural process.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: Morality is historically and socially relative, and recognizing that fact places responsibility for moral judgments and choices on human decision-makers rather than claimed divine authority.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-05.proposition: The suffering of infants from cancer creates a direct tension with the existence of a God described as omnipotent, omniscient, and wholly benevolent.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-10.proposition: An omnipotent God could realize any proposed later or eternal good without childhood leukemia, so unknown future benefits do not explain why such suffering is necessary.

chunk-004:c004-06.proposition: Human concern for suffering arises from evolved social empathy shared with other animals, providing a natural account of compassion and cooperative conduct without divine moral grounding.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Deducing a timeless, spaceless, law-transcending deity requires an independent evidential basis, and unexplained phenomena alone provide no such basis.
